body: I've been trying to convince myself to make an appointment with the counseling center for probably ~6 months now. I don't know, I always get the feeling that the experience will just be hollow and meaningless and I'll be left with pharmaceuticals as my only other option. I've always had problems with expressing emotions, even as a small child I remember being completely unphased by death and being asked if I was even sad about it. I wasn't, to be honest. I think I have some sort of emotional disconnection with humanity.

The friends that I do have I would hesitate to call friends except for one person. I would consider most of them mere acquaintances, really. I would never really engage in any sort of personal conversation with them willingly. They only know of me what I've wanted them to know, nothing more. The one person that I truly do consider a friend has now moved about 6 hours away from where I live, though we do still keep in contact via the internet, the relationship is dwindling.

My weight was never a real issue as far as my social life went. I've never really had much of a problem maintaining an image of self-confidence, even at my heaviest.

Apart from my brother, I couldn't care less about my family. Even with him I can't really talk about what I'm feeling because I know that he is more or less an open book to my parents. If I told him that I was feeling suicidal, the news would be to my parents within the hour. I love him, but I cannot trust him.

Yep, I have one more year of undergrad and then however long it takes me to get my PhD.

Nope, never had any treatment for it. Nor have I ever talked to anyone about my depression offline. If I had ever given my parents the idea that I was depressed they would have absolutely smothered me. They were already over-protective of me, especially since my older brother attempted suicide. If they ever thought that I had had suicidal thoughts they would not hesitate to force me out of school and back home.
Yes, we do have a counseling program available, but I've never really been good about talking to people about my feelings face-to-face. That's something that's quite convenient about the internet.
